construct: ATP2C1 encodes hSPCA1, an ATP-powered pump that transports calcium and manganese into the Golgi apparatus. Loss of functional hSPCA1 disrupts Golgi calcium storage in keratinocytes, impairing cell adhesion and making the epidermis fragile in areas exposed to heat, moisture, and friction.

distractor_audit.distractor: ATP-dependent transport of calcium into the endoplasmic reticulum
distractor_audit.rationale: SERCA2, encoded by ATP2A2, is an ATP-dependent calcium pump of the endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum. ATP2C1 instead encodes hSPCA1, which pumps calcium into the Golgi apparatus.

distractor_audit.distractor: Voltage-gated transport of calcium into cells across the plasma membrane
distractor_audit.rationale: CaV1.2, encoded by CACNA1C, is a voltage-gated plasma-membrane calcium channel that permits calcium entry into cells; it is not the ATP2C1-encoded Golgi ATPase.

distractor_audit.distractor: ATP-dependent transport of copper within the Golgi and into biliary secretory vesicles
distractor_audit.rationale: ATP7B is a copper-transporting P-type ATPase that functions in the Golgi and can traffic to vesicles for biliary copper elimination; ATP2C1 instead transports calcium and manganese into the Golgi.

distractor_audit.distractor: Channel-mediated transport of chloride across the plasma membrane
distractor_audit.rationale: CFTR is a plasma-membrane chloride channel; it does not perform ATP-dependent sequestration of calcium into the Golgi.

educational_objective_text: Connect Hailey-Hailey disease caused by ATP2C1 variants to defective ATP-dependent calcium transport into the Golgi apparatus.

option_audit.correct_concept: ATP-dependent transport of calcium into the Golgi apparatus

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: ATP2C1 encodes hSPCA1, an ATP-powered secretory-pathway calcium/manganese pump that transports calcium into the Golgi apparatus. ATP2C1 loss impairs Golgi calcium storage and keratinocyte adhesion in Hailey-Hailey disease.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ATP2A2/SERCA2 is the ER/SR calcium ATPase; CACNA1C/CaV1.2 is a voltage-gated plasma-membrane calcium channel; ATP7B is a Golgi copper-transporting P-type ATPase that can traffic to vesicles for biliary copper elimination; CFTR is a plasma-membrane chloride channel.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Because ATP2C1 is explicitly identified in the stem, only ATP-dependent calcium transport into the Golgi matches the encoded protein's compartment, substrate, and energy mechanism.
